subject: 90 m
value: Maximum length of a copper permanent link (the fixed cabling that gets certified).
quote: The maximum permitted length of the permanent link is 90 meters.

subject: 100 m
value: Maximum length of a copper channel: up to 90 m of cabling plus no more than 10 m of patch cords.
quote: Industry standards limit the overall length of a channel to 100 meters, including up to 90 meters of cabling and no more than 10 meters of patch cords.

subject: 4x OD
value: Minimum bend radius of unshielded twisted-pair (UTP) cable: 4 times the cable outer diameter.
quote: UTP should not be bent tighter than four times the cable's outer diameter

subject: 8x OD
value: Minimum bend radius of shielded twisted-pair cable: 8 times the cable outer diameter.
quote: shielded cables require at least eight times

subject: 25 lbf (110 N)
value: Maximum pulling tension on 4-pair copper data cable.
quote: TIA-568.2-D limits pulling tension for 4-pair copper to 25 pounds-force (110 newtons).

subject: 13 mm (1/2 in)
value: Maximum untwist of a pair at a Cat6 termination.
quote: No more than 13 millimetres, or half an inch, from the termination point

subject: 12 in power/data separation
value: Minimum separation between power and data cabling (TIA-569); where they must meet, cross at 90 degrees.
quote: ANSI/TIA-569-D specifies a minimum of 12 inches, roughly 300 millimetres, between power and data cabling.

subject: 5 ft J-hook spacing
value: Maximum spacing between J-hooks (1.5 m); 4 to 5 ft is typical.
quote: The hard ceiling on spacing is 5 feet (60 inches) between supports.

subject: 12 in J-hook sag
value: Maximum cable sag between two J-hooks.
quote: Cable should not droop more than about 12 inches between two supports.

subject: 40% J-hook fill
value: Fill limit of a J-hook (or tray) cross-sectional area for data cable.
quote: keep fill at or below roughly 40% of the hook's cross-sectional area

subject: 24 cables per bundle
value: BICSI guidance on maximum bundle size unless the cable is certified for larger bundles.
quote: BICSI guidance is to limit bundles to 24 cables or fewer unless the cable is certified for larger bundles.

subject: 250 MHz
value: Certification frequency range for Category 6 (Cat5e 100 MHz, Cat6A 500 MHz).
quote: up to 100 MHz for Category 5e, 250 MHz for Category 6, and 500 MHz for Category 6A

subject: 0.75 dB
value: TIA-568 maximum loss of a mated fiber connector pair.
quote: (0.75 max per EIA/TIA 568)

subject: 0.3 dB
value: TIA-568 maximum loss of a fiber splice (single-mode fusion splices are typically about 0.15 dB).
quote: (0.3 max per EIA/TIA 568)

subject: 3.5 dB/km
value: TIA-568 maximum attenuation of multimode fiber at 850 nm (1.5 dB/km at 1300 nm).
quote: (3.5 and 1.5 dB/km max per EIA/TIA 568)

subject: 1.0 dB/km
value: TIA-568 maximum attenuation of single-mode fiber in premises cabling (0.5 dB/km outside plant).
quote: 1.0 dB/km for premises/0.5 dB/km at either wavelength for outside plant max per EIA/TIA 568

subject: 20x OD
value: Minimum fiber cable bend radius while pulling (under tension).
quote: the minimum bend radius under tension during pulling is 20 times the diameter of the cable

subject: 10x OD
value: Minimum fiber cable bend radius after installation (no tension).
quote: the minimum recommended long term bend radius is 10 times the cable diameter

subject: 1 km OTDR launch cable
value: Recommended minimum launch cable for long-distance single-mode OTDR tests.
quote: For singlemode long distance tests, at least a 1 km launch cable is recommended.

subject: 0.008 lb/cmil
value: Maximum allowable conductor stress for soft copper: max tension = 0.008 x circular mils (4/0 Cu, 211,600 cmil = about 1,693 lb). The lowest limit wins.
quote: All Copper Soft 0.008

subject: 10,000 lb pulling eye
value: Maximum tension on a pulling eye: the eye manufacturer's rating or 10,000 lb, whichever is less.
quote: Do not exceed the allowable tension stated by the manufacturer of the pulling eye or 10,000 pounds, whichever is less.

subject: 1,000 lb basket grip
value: Conservative tension limit for a basket grip.
quote: Traditional conservative practices limit the allowable tension of a basket grip to 1,000 pounds.

subject: 4x / 5x / 6x tray cable bend
value: Type TC tray cable minimum bending radius: 4 x OD up to 1 in, 5 x for 1 to 2 in, 6 x above 2 in (12 x with metallic shielding).
quote: a) Diameter 1.0 inch or less 4 b) Diameter between 1.0 inch to 2.0 inches 5 c) Diameter larger than 2.0 inches 6

subject: 4/0 AWG single layer
value: Multiconductor cables 4/0 AWG and larger in tray: single layer, sum of diameters no more than the tray width (NEC 392.22).
quote: Cables 4/0 AWG and larger: The sum of the cable diameters can't exceed the tray width, and the cables must lie in a single layer.

subject: 50% / 40% control cable tray fill
value: Control and signal cable only: 50% fill in ladder or ventilated tray, 40% in solid bottom tray.
quote: Fill is limited to 50 percent of the tray's inside cross-sectional area in ladder or ventilated tray, and 40 percent in solid bottom tray.

subject: 1 megohm per 1,000 V
value: Megger rule of thumb for minimum insulation resistance (never below 1 megohm); the project spec sets the real pass value.
quote: Insulation resistance should be approximately one megohm for each 1,000 volts of operating voltage, with a minimum value of one megohm.

subject: 500 / 1,000 V DC test
value: Common DC insulation test voltages for 440 to 550 V equipment (600 V cable is typically tested at 1,000 V DC).
quote: 440 to 550 volts 500 and 1,000 volts

subject: 24 h heated storage
value: Cable to be installed in cold weather is kept in heated storage at least 24 hours first.
quote: they should be kept in heated storage for at least 24 hours before installation

subject: 1.2 cal/cm2
value: Incident energy at the arc flash boundary (NFPA 70E): beyond it, no second degree burn.
quote: where the incident energy equals 1.2 cal/cm2

subject: 4 / 8 / 25 / 40 cal/cm2
value: Minimum arc rating of clothing for arc flash PPE Categories 1, 2, 3 and 4.
quote: Arc Flash PPE Category 1 Arc-Rated Clothing, Minimum Arc Rating of 4 cal/cm2

subject: 0.02-0.06 inWC cleanroom cascade
value: Typical pressure difference between a cleanroom zone and the adjacent space (5 to 15 Pa).
quote: Typical cascade 0.02-0.06 inWC (5-15 Pa).

subject: 6 months CCTV maintenance
value: Schedule camera maintenance (clean domes, check cables) at least every six months.
quote: maintenance should be scheduled at least every six months

subject: 70% of heat deaths in week 1
value: Over 70 percent of heat-related deaths happen during a worker's first week; almost half on the first day.
quote: Over 70 percent of heat-related deaths occur during a worker's first week

subject: 20 percent first day
value: Rule of 20 percent: a new worker works only 20% of the normal duration in the heat on day one, building up over 1 to 2 weeks.
quote: New workers should work only 20 percent of the normal duration on their first day.

subject: 10% IPA / 90% DI water
value: Wipe-down solution for approved items before they go into the cleanroom (with gloves and safety glasses).
quote: wiped down prior to entry with a solution of 10% IPA and 90% DI H2O
